<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds `MooncakePullConnector`, a READ-mode sibling of `MooncakeConnector`: the decoder reads the prefiller's KV cache over the Mooncake TransferEngine instead of the prefiller writing into the decoder's registered memory. It is registered under its own name, and `MooncakeConnector` keeps its wire format, metadata and behavior.

Part of the Mooncake connector roadmap in [#60523](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60523).

## Claims

- **New connector with decoder-side reads.** The prefiller holds its KV blocks, publishes its address book and block ids, and releases a request once every reader reports the read finished; the decoder issues `batch_transfer_sync_read` at its own scheduling pace. Select it with `--kv-connector MooncakePullConnector` on both sides, using the existing proxy and `kv_transfer_config` fields; `KV_CONNECTOR=MooncakePullConnector` picks it in the example script.
- **KV layout on the handshake, not on every batch.** The decoder fetches each peer worker's layout once and caches it, keyed by a `layout_id` so a restarted peer is noticed and re-fetched. Per-request messages carry block ids only: with 146 registered regions and a batch of 8 requests × 4 blocks, the pull request payload is 309 B against 7297 B for the push handshake payload, of which 7164 B is the address book.
- **Compatibility-hash isolation.** Both sides hash model, dtype, KV heads/head size/layers, KV cache dtype, attention backend, HMA, EAGLE/MTP configuration, connector version and transfer mode, and compare the digests during the handshake. TP size, block size and KV cache layout stay out of the hash and are validated against the peer's address book instead, which keeps heterogeneous TP working. A mismatched pair fails the request with a message naming the reason.
- **Pull connector reuses the existing machinery.** `MooncakePullConnector` subclasses `MooncakeConnector` and swaps only the worker, mirroring `NixlPullConnector` and `NixlPushConnector`; scheduler, request metadata and registered regions are shared, and reads are planned in `mooncake/transfer_plan.py` from the same region helpers the push path uses.
- **Push behavior preserved.** `MooncakeXferMetadata`, `MooncakeXferResponse` and the send path are unchanged; the push connector gains only the seams both modes share (`_handle_side_channel_message`, `_send_side_channel_error`, `_send_idle`), the connector name in its bootstrap registration, and an aborted-transfer event its own path ignores.

## Validation

Unit tests, on the commit in this PR:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_pull_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_stats.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py
# 188 passed
```

`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_pull_connector.py` runs two workers against each other over the real ZMQ side channel and bootstrap server, with the transfer engine replaced by a byte-copying stand-in that keeps the memory-registration table, so a descriptor pointing outside registered memory fails the test. It covers byte-for-byte reads, the address book fetched once per peer and re-fetched after a peer restart, heterogeneous TP (one decoder rank reading two prefiller ranks), release on a decoder-side prefix hit, rejection of an incompatible peer (compatibility hash, block size, connector mode), reader failure and abort releasing the prefiller's blocks, and prefiller timeout failing the reader.

Serving validation on an 8×H20 node, same-host P/D pair over RDMA (both sides log `The Mooncake Transfer Engine is using rdma as its protocol`), driven through the example proxy with three greedy prompts per configuration and every completion compared character by character:

| Configuration | pull vs. non-disaggregated | push vs. non-disaggregated | pull vs. push |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| dense 0.5B, P tp=1 / D tp=1 | identical | identical | identical |
| hybrid 2B, P tp=1 / D tp=1 | identical | identical | identical |
| dense 0.5B, P tp=2 / D tp=1 | identical | n/a | n/a |

The worker logs show which side moves the bytes:

```text
# decoder, pull mode
DEBUG mooncake_pull_connector.py] Reading kv_caches for {'cmpl-...'} from producer worker tcp://172.31.32.3:45359
DEBUG mooncake_pull_connector.py] Reading from 172.31.32.3:15558 done, took 0.00605 (24 descriptors, 1769472 bytes)

# prefiller, push mode (same instrumentation, same run shape)
DEBUG mooncake_connector.py]      Sending to 172.31.32.3:16093 done, took 0.00833
```

The three dense prompts read 24 descriptors each: 1.69 MiB in 6.0 ms, 1.69 MiB in 0.35 ms (prefix-cached), and 576 KiB in 0.68 ms. The hybrid prompts read 24 descriptors and 27 MiB each, in 7.1 ms, 1.1 ms and 1.0 ms. The prefiller log in pull mode contains no transfer line at all, while in push mode it logs one write per prompt, and neither worker logs an error.

## Details

**Protocol.** The decoder sends `MooncakePullRequest` (protocol marker, compatibility hash, reader identity, `{request id: (transfer id, needs bytes)}`, and whether it wants the layout); the prefiller answers with `MooncakePullResponse` (layout and/or producer block ids per request, or an error); the decoder reads the blocks, then reports `MooncakePullDone` and waits for `MooncakePullAck`. The prefiller holds blocks from the moment it hands out block ids until every expected reader reports in. The expected reader count comes from the same `TransferTopology` rules the push connector uses for its TP/PP fan-out, and a request that no reader takes is released after `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`.

**Read planning.** `plan_read_block_descriptors` turns one request's producer and consumer block ids into remote and local descriptors using the registered regions, the KV group identity, the Mamba/GDN placeholder rule, per-side logical-to-kernel block expansion and contiguous-run coalescing; it is the read-side counterpart of the push worker's descriptor loop, and region alignment and asymmetric-TP validation reuse the existing helpers.

**Who validates what.** Handing out block ids lets a reader slice the prefiller's cache by KV head, so the head-resharding check (padded pages, NVFP4) runs on the prefiller, which is the only side holding the registered layer specs, using the TP degree the reader reports. The decoder keeps the checks it can make from the address book alone: block size, physical blocks per logical block, MLA/Mamba flags, layout id, and the region-length relations of asymmetric TP.

**Failure handling.** Read and planning failures go through the connector's existing failure path (`_handle_failed_recv`, `get_block_ids_with_load_errors`), so the scheduler recomputes or fails the request according to `kv_load_failure_policy` and the prefiller releases the blocks of a failed read. The decoder reports a batch it abandons (rejected layout, compatibility mismatch, error response) the same way it reports a finished one, because the prefiller handed out those block ids before the decoder could validate the response. A prefiller that drops a request (abort or its own expiry) sets the new `aborted` event so a waiting reader fails immediately instead of waiting out its own timeout, and a reader that disappears after taking block ids stops holding them once `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` passes.

**Mixed pairs.** A decoder running the pull connector that finds a prefiller registered as `MooncakeConnector` (or as nothing at all, since an unset name means a prefiller predating connector names) fails the request at discovery with a message naming both connectors. The bootstrap server refuses to register two different connector names under one `dp_rank`.

**Not included, tracked elsewhere in [#60523](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60523):** layerwise transfer overlap (Phase 4), DCP/PCP and the wider heterogeneous-TP work (Phase 3), and de-HTTP-izing bootstrap (Phase 2 evaluation item). `kv_both` inherits the push scheduler's existing role semantics and is not exercised by tests.

**Why this is not a duplicate:** no open or merged PR adds a pull connector for the Mooncake P2P path (checked by name and by search); the closest open work fixes failure reporting on the existing push connector, which this connector already routes through. Sending the KV layout once per peer for the push handshake already landed on `main`; this change applies the same idea in the read direction.

**Validation limits.** The Mooncake transfer engine is not available in CI, so the unit tests use the byte-copying stand-in described above and GPU/RDMA validation happens outside CI. The serving runs above used a same-host P/D pair; a cross-host pair was not validated for this PR.

+class FakeCopyEngine:

+    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):

+        )

+        ):

+"""Compatibility factors for the Mooncake P2P connectors.
+
+The push and pull connectors hand each other KV cache bytes, so they must agree
+on the model, the KV cache format, and the protocol. Both sides hash those
+factors at startup and compare the digests during the handshake, which turns a
+mismatched deployment into one failed request with a reason instead of a
+transfer neither side can interpret.
+"""
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+# Increment this whenever an incompatible change lands in either connector's
+# handshake or wire format, so mismatched peers fail the handshake instead of
+# transferring bytes neither side can read.
+#
+# History:
+#   1: pull-mode handshake (address book, block ids, completion report)
+MOONCAKE_CONNECTOR_VERSION: int = 1
+
+
+def get_speculative_compatibility_factors(
+    vllm_config: "VllmConfig",
+) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
+    """Compatibility factors of a speculator that moves KV state between peers."""
+    speculative_config = vllm_config.speculative_config
+    if speculative_config is None or not speculative_config.use_eagle():
+        return None
+
+    draft_model_config = speculative_config.draft_model_config
+    assert draft_model_config is not None
+    auxiliary_layer_ids = getattr(
+        draft_model_config.hf_config,
+        "eagle_aux_hidden_state_layer_ids",
+        None,
+    )
+    # kv_cache_dtype defaults to None, meaning "inherit from the target model".
+    # Resolve it so an explicit setting on one side and inheritance on the other
+    # do not look like a mismatch.
+    kv_cache_dtype = (
+        speculative_config.kv_cache_dtype or vllm_config.cache_config.cache_dtype
+    )
+    return {
+        "method": speculative_config.method,
+        "model": draft_model_config.model,
+        "revision": draft_model_config.revision,
+        "code_revision": draft_model_config.code_revision,
+        "parallel_drafting": speculative_config.parallel_drafting,
+        "kv_cache_dtype": str(kv_cache_dtype),
+        "auxiliary_layer_ids": (
+            tuple(auxiliary_layer_ids) if auxiliary_layer_ids is not None else None
+        ),
+    }
+
+
+def compute_mooncake_compatibility_hash(
+    vllm_config: "VllmConfig",
+    attn_backend_name: str,
+    transfer_mode: str = "pull",
+) -> str:
+    """Hash the factors that decide whether two Mooncake peers can transfer KV.
+
+    Factors included:
+    - vLLM version and Mooncake connector version
+    - Model architecture (name, dtype, KV heads, head size, layers)
+    - KV cache format (dtype, hybrid KV cache manager)
+    - Attention backend
+    - EAGLE/MTP configuration that affects transferred state
+    - Transfer mode (pull vs push)
+
+    The transfer mode is included because the pull (READ) and push (WRITE)
+    connectors use incompatible transfer protocols; a pull connector and a push
+    connector must never complete a handshake with each other.
+
+    Factors like tensor_parallel_size, block_size and kv_cache_layout are
+    validated against the peer's address book at runtime and stay out of the
+    hash to support heterogeneous deployments.
+
+    Args:
+        vllm_config: Configuration of this instance.
+        attn_backend_name: Name of the attention backend holding the cache.
+        transfer_mode: "pull" or "push".
+
+    Returns:
+        SHA-256 hex digest of the factors above.
+
+    """
+    from vllm import __version__ as vllm_version
+    from vllm.config.utils import hash_factors
+
+    model_config = vllm_config.model_config
+    cache_config = vllm_config.cache_config
+    factors = {
+        "vllm_version": vllm_version,
+        "mooncake_connector_version": MOONCAKE_CONNECTOR_VERSION,
+        "model": model_config.model,
+        "dtype": str(model_config.dtype),
+        "num_kv_heads": model_config.get_total_num_kv_heads(),
+        "head_size": model_config.get_head_size(),
+        "num_hidden_layers": model_config.get_total_num_hidden_layers(),
+        "attn_backend_name": attn_backend_name,
+        "cache_dtype": str(cache_config.cache_dtype),
+        "is_hma_enabled": (
+            not vllm_config.scheduler_config.disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager
+        ),
+        "speculative_config": get_speculative_compatibility_factors(vllm_config),
+        "transfer_mode": transfer_mode,
+    }
+    compat_hash = hash_factors(factors)
+    logger.debug(
+        "Mooncake compatibility hash: %s (model=%s, dtype=%s, num_kv_heads=%d, "
+        "cache_dtype=%s, attn_backend=%s, transfer_mode=%s)",
+        compat_hash,
+        factors["model"],
+        factors["dtype"],
+        factors["num_kv_heads"],
+        factors["cache_dtype"],
+        factors["attn_backend_name"],
+        transfer_mode,
+    )
+    return compat_hash

+"""Mooncake pull connector: the decoder reads the prefill KV cache itself.
+
+`MooncakeConnector` has the prefiller write into the decoder's registered
+memory, so every request batch carries the decoder's KV region table to the
+prefiller. This connector turns the transfer around: the decoder asks each
+paired prefiller worker for its KV address book (once per peer, then cached)
+and for the block ids of the requests it is about to read, then reads the bytes
+with `batch_transfer_sync_read` at its own scheduling pace. The prefiller holds
+the blocks until every reader reports the read as finished.
+

+regions; only the transfer direction and the side-channel messages differ.

+    transfer_ids: list[TransferId]

+    msgspec.Struct,
+    omit_defaults=True,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+):

+    layout_id: str | None = None
+    compat_hash: str | None = None

+    err_reqs: list[ReqId] | None = None

+    msgspec.Struct,
+    omit_defaults=True,  # type: ignore[call-arg]

+class MooncakePullConnector(MooncakeConnector):
+    """Mooncake P2P connector in READ mode.
+
+    Same scheduler, metadata and registered regions as `MooncakeConnector`;
+    only the worker differs, because the decoder reads the prefiller's KV cache
+    instead of the prefiller writing into the decoder's memory.
+    """
+
+    def _build_worker(
+        self, vllm_config: VllmConfig, kv_cache_config: "KVCacheConfig"
+    ) -> "MooncakePullConnectorWorker":
+        assert self.engine_id is not None
+        return MooncakePullConnectorWorker(vllm_config, self.engine_id, kv_cache_config)
+
+    def get_kv_connector_stats(self) -> KVConnectorStats | None:
+        """Return worker-local transfer stats since the last call.
+
+        Note the P/D asymmetry of the pull direction: the decoder performs the
+        read, so transfer latency, bytes and descriptor counts are recorded on
+        the decoder worker, while the prefiller records the failures it observes
+        and the requests whose blocks expired before any reader came.
+        """
+        return super().get_kv_connector_stats()
+
+
+class MooncakePullConnectorWorker(MooncakeConnectorWorker):
+    """Worker-side implementation of the pull connector.
+
+    On the prefiller the worker holds KV blocks and hands out its address book
+    and block ids. On the decoder it reads those blocks into its own cache and
+    reports completion, which releases the prefiller's blocks.
+    """
+
+    connector_name = "MooncakePullConnector"
+    # A prefiller that never reports a connector name predates the pull
+    # connector, so a reader cannot tell whether it speaks this protocol.
+    allow_missing_peer_connector = False
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+        engine_id: str,
+        kv_cache_config: "KVCacheConfig",
+    ):
+        super().__init__(vllm_config, engine_id, kv_cache_config)
+
+        self._pull_message_decoder = msgspec.msgpack.Decoder(PullMessage)
+        self._pull_response_decoder = msgspec.msgpack.Decoder(MooncakePullResponse)
+        self._pull_ack_decoder = msgspec.msgpack.Decoder(MooncakePullAck)
+        # Both sides hash the same transfer-relevant configuration and compare
+        # it during the handshake, so a peer that cannot interpret these bytes
+        # is refused before any transfer starts.
+        self._compat_hash = compute_mooncake_compatibility_hash(
+            vllm_config=vllm_config,
+            attn_backend_name=self.attn_backends[0].get_name(),
+            transfer_mode="pull",
+        )
+
+        # Prefiller side: this worker's own address book, built on first use,
+        # plus the readers that were handed block ids but have not reported the
+        # read as finished.
+        self._layout: MooncakePullLayout | None = None
+        self._handed_out_readers: dict[TransferId, set[ReaderKey]] = {}
+        self._handed_out_at: dict[TransferId, float] = {}
+        self._done_readers: dict[TransferId, set[ReaderKey]] = {}
+
+        # Decoder side: peer worker address -> its cached address book.
+        self._peer_layouts: dict[str, MooncakePullLayout] = {}
+
+        if self.is_kv_producer:
+            return
+        # The read blocks its calling thread, so it runs on a pool. Each pool
+        # thread must be bound to the correct device, because that binding is
+        # thread-local.
+        self._reader_executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(
+            max_workers=self.num_sender_workers,
+            thread_name_prefix="vllm-mooncake-reader",
+            initializer=self._bind_sender_thread_device,
+        )
+
+    def shutdown(self):
+        reader_executor = getattr(self, "_reader_executor", None)
+        if reader_executor is not None:
+            reader_executor.shutdown(wait=False)
+        # A socket parked in a receive never lets the context terminate, and the
+        # reader holds one open, so close every socket before the base class
+        # stops the loops.
+        self.async_zmq_ctx.destroy(linger=0)
+        super().shutdown()
+
+    ############################################################
+    # Prefiller side: hand out blocks and address book
+    ############################################################
+
+    def _get_layout(self) -> MooncakePullLayout:
+        """This worker's address book, hashed so readers notice a new one."""
+        if self._layout is None:
+            layout = MooncakePullLayout(
+                engine_id=self.engine_id,
+                hostname=self.hostname,
+                rpc_port=self.rpc_port,
+                tp_rank=self.tp_rank,
+                pp_rank=self.pp_rank,
+                tp_size=self.tp_size,
+                pp_size=self.pp_size,
+                block_size=self.block_size,
+                physical_blocks_per_logical=(
+                    self._physical_blocks_per_logical_kv_block
+                ),
+                use_mla=self.use_mla,
+                has_mamba=self.kv_cache_config.has_mamba_layers,
+                producer_cache_replicated=self._producer_cache_is_replicated(),
+                kv_caches_base_addr=self.kv_caches_base_addr,
+                block_lens=self.block_len_per_layer,
+                kv_block_lens=self.kv_block_len_per_layer,
+                layer_names=self.registered_layer_names,
+                layer_indices=self.registered_layer_indices,
+                group_indices=self.registered_group_indices,
+                shared_group_ids=[list(groups) for groups in self.region_shared_groups],
+                row_offsets=list(self.region_row_offsets),
+            )
+            layout.layout_id = safe_hash(
+                self._encoder.encode(layout), usedforsecurity=False
+            ).hexdigest()[:16]
+            self._layout = layout
+        return self._layout
+
+    def _resolve_expected_readers(
+        self, send_meta: SendBlockMeta, reader_tp_size: int, reader_pp_size: int
+    ) -> None:
+        """How many reader workers a set of blocks is served to."""
+        expected = len(self.transfer_topo.handshake_target_ranks(reader_tp_size))
+        if reader_pp_size > 1 and reader_pp_size != self.pp_size:
+            # Every reader PP stage reads every producer stage, including peers
+            # with no shared layers.
+            expected *= reader_pp_size
+        if send_meta.need_send and send_meta.need_send != expected:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"Transfer {send_meta.transfer_id} is read by "
+                f"{send_meta.need_send} workers, but the reader topology "
+                f"(tp={reader_tp_size}, pp={reader_pp_size}) implies {expected}."
+            )
+        send_meta.need_send = expected
+
+    def _complete_transfer_if_read_by_all(self, send_meta: SendBlockMeta) -> None:
+        if not send_meta.p_req_id:
+            # The prefiller's own scheduler has not registered this transfer
+            # yet; `record_send_reqs` completes it once it does.
+            return
+        if not send_meta.need_send:
+            return
+        if len(self._done_readers.get(send_meta.transfer_id, ())) < send_meta.need_send:
+            return
+        transfer_id = send_meta.transfer_id
+        if self.reqs_need_send.pop(transfer_id, None) is None:
+            return
+        self._handed_out_readers.pop(transfer_id, None)
+        self._handed_out_at.pop(transfer_id, None)
+        self._done_readers.pop(transfer_id, None)
+        self.finished_sending_reqs.add(send_meta.p_req_id)
+
+    def _mark_reader_done(
+        self, send_meta: SendBlockMeta, readers_key: ReaderKey
+    ) -> None:
+        transfer_id = send_meta.transfer_id
+        self._handed_out_readers.get(transfer_id, set()).discard(readers_key)
+        self._done_readers.setdefault(transfer_id, set()).add(readers_key)
+        self._complete_transfer_if_read_by_all(send_meta)
+
+    async def fetch_finished_sending_reqs(self) -> set[ReqId]:
+        """Report released transfers, and forget the ones already released.
+
+        A transfer can leave `reqs_need_send` through completion or through the
+        prefiller's expiry. The reader bookkeeping has to follow both, or a
+        released transfer would keep looking like one a reader still holds.
+        """
+        finished = await super().fetch_finished_sending_reqs()
+        for transfer_id in list(self._handed_out_readers):
+            if transfer_id in self.reqs_need_send:
+                continue
+            self._handed_out_readers.pop(transfer_id, None)
+            self._handed_out_at.pop(transfer_id, None)
+            self._done_readers.pop(transfer_id, None)
+        return finished
+
+    def _send_idle(self, transfer_id: TransferId) -> bool:
+        """Whether the blocks of a transfer are free to be released.
+
+        Blocks whose ids were handed out stay held while a reader may still be
+        reading them. A reader that never reports back would hold them forever,
+        so a hand-out older than the abort timeout counts as gone.
+        """
+        if not self._handed_out_readers.get(transfer_id):
+            return True
+        handed_out_at = self._handed_out_at.get(transfer_id)
+        if handed_out_at is None:
+            return False
+        return (
+            time.perf_counter() - handed_out_at
+            > envs.VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT
+        )
+
+    async def record_send_reqs(self, metadata: MooncakeConnectorMetadata) -> None:
+        """Register the prefiller's finished requests, then re-check completion.
+
+        A reader with a full local prefix hit reports completion before the
+        prefiller's own scheduler registers the transfer, so completion has to
+        be re-checked once the blocks show up.
+        """
+        await super().record_send_reqs(metadata)
+        for send_meta in list(self.reqs_need_send.values()):
+            self._complete_transfer_if_read_by_all(send_meta)
+
+    async def _handle_side_channel_message(
+        self, identity: bytes, payload: bytes, sock: zmq.asyncio.Socket
+    ) -> None:
+        try:
+            message = self._pull_message_decoder.decode(payload)
+        except msgspec.DecodeError as e:
+            # Name the mismatch for the peer instead of handing it a raw
+            # decoding failure.
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "The peer sent a message that is not a Mooncake pull message, "
+                "so the push and pull connectors are mixed on this P/D pair: "
+                f"{e}"
+            ) from e
+        self._check_protocol(message.protocol)
+        if isinstance(message, MooncakePullRequest):
+            await self._handle_pull_request(identity, sock, message)
+        else:
+            await self._handle_read_done(identity, sock, message)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _check_protocol(protocol: str) -> None:
+        if protocol != PULL_PROTOCOL:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"Unsupported pull protocol {protocol!r}, expected {PULL_PROTOCOL!r}."
+            )
+
+    def _compat_mismatch_reason(self, peer_hash: str | None) -> str:
+        return (
+            "Mooncake pull transfer refused: the peer configuration is "
+            f"incompatible with this one (peer compat hash {peer_hash}, local "
+            f"{self._compat_hash}). Both sides must run the same model, dtype, KV "
+            "cache dtype, attention backend, speculative configuration and "
+            "connector version."
+        )
+
+    async def _send_side_channel_error(
+        self, identity: bytes, sock: zmq.asyncio.Socket, err_msg: str
+    ) -> None:
+        # Reply in the push connector's error envelope: a peer that runs the
+        # push connector fails its requests with this message instead of
+        # waiting for its timeout, and the message names the mismatch.
+        response = MooncakeXferResponse(
+            status=MooncakeXferResponseStatus.ERROR, err_msg=err_msg
+        )
+        await sock.send_multipart((identity, self._encoder.encode(response)))
+
+    async def _wait_for_blocks(
+        self, d_req_id: ReqId, send_meta: SendBlockMeta
+    ) -> tuple[ReqId, SendBlockMeta]:
+        """Wait for the prefiller's blocks, or for the request being dropped."""
+        wait_tasks = {
+            asyncio.create_task(send_meta.ready.wait()),
+            asyncio.create_task(send_meta.aborted.wait()),
+        }
+        try:
+            await asyncio.wait(wait_tasks, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
+        finally:
+            for task in wait_tasks:
+                task.cancel()
+        return d_req_id, send_meta
+
+    async def _handle_pull_request(
+        self,
+        identity: bytes,
+        sock: zmq.asyncio.Socket,
+        request: MooncakePullRequest,
+    ) -> None:
+        if request.compat_hash != self._compat_hash:
+            # Answer in this protocol so the reader reports the real reason
+            # instead of an undecodable response.
+            response = MooncakePullResponse(
+                status=MooncakeXferResponseStatus.ERROR,
+                compat_hash=self._compat_hash,
+                err_msg=self._compat_mismatch_reason(request.compat_hash),
+            )
+            await sock.send_multipart((identity, self._encoder.encode(response)))
+            return
+
+        readers_key: ReaderKey = (request.engine_id, request.tp_rank, request.pp_rank)
+
+        # Handing out block ids lets the reader slice this worker's cache by KV
+        # head, so the reader's TP degree has to be a layout this cache can
+        # serve. Only this side holds the registered layer specs the check
+        # needs, so it runs here.
+        head_err = self._validate_head_resharding_layout(
+            request.tp_size, self._local_transfer_regions()
+        )
+        if head_err is not None:
+            response = MooncakePullResponse(
+                status=MooncakeXferResponseStatus.ERROR,
+                compat_hash=self._compat_hash,
+                err_msg=head_err,
+            )
+            await sock.send_multipart((identity, self._encoder.encode(response)))
+            return
+
+        layout = self._get_layout() if request.want_layout else None
+
+        resolved: dict[ReqId, tuple[TransferId, list[list[int]]]] = {}
+        err_reqs: list[ReqId] = []
+        err_msg: str | None = None
+        pending: list[tuple[ReqId, SendBlockMeta]] = []
+
+        for d_req_id, (transfer_id, needs_data) in request.reqs.items():
+            send_meta = self.reqs_need_send.get(transfer_id)
+            if send_meta is None:
+                # This reader may pair with the prefiller rank before its
+                # scheduler registered the request; hold it until the blocks
+                # show up.
+                send_meta = SendBlockMeta(
+                    p_req_id="",
+                    transfer_id=transfer_id,
+                    local_block_ids=[],
+                    ready=asyncio.Event(),
+                )
+                self.reqs_need_send[transfer_id] = send_meta
+            self._resolve_expected_readers(send_meta, request.tp_size, request.pp_size)
+
+            if not needs_data:
+                # A reader with a full local prefix hit only needs the
+                # prefiller to release the request, which happens as soon as
+                # it is done.
+                resolved[d_req_id] = (transfer_id, [])
+                self._mark_reader_done(send_meta, readers_key)
+                continue
+            pending.append((d_req_id, send_meta))
+
+        # One waiter per request that still needs its blocks, reused across
+        # responses, so a batch that becomes ready piecemeal never piles up
+        # waiters for requests it is already waiting on.
+        waiters: dict[asyncio.Task, tuple[ReqId, SendBlockMeta]] = {
+            asyncio.create_task(self._wait_for_blocks(d_req_id, send_meta)): (
+                d_req_id,
+                send_meta,
+            )
+            for d_req_id, send_meta in pending
+        }
+        try:
+            while True:
+                status = (
+                    MooncakeXferResponseStatus.FINISH
+                    if not waiters
+                    else MooncakeXferResponseStatus.CONTINUE
+                )
+                response = MooncakePullResponse(
+                    status=status,
+                    layout_id=self._get_layout().layout_id,
+                    compat_hash=self._compat_hash,
+                    layout=layout,
+                    resolved=resolved or None,
+                    err_reqs=err_reqs or None,
+                    err_msg=err_msg,
+                )
+                await sock.send_multipart((identity, self._encoder.encode(response)))
+
+                # The address book travels with the first response only.
+                layout = None
+                resolved = {}
+                err_reqs = []
+                err_msg = None
+                if not waiters:
+                    break
+
+                done, _ = await asyncio.wait(
+                    waiters,
+                    timeout=envs.VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT,
+                    return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED,
+                )
+                if not done:
+                    err_reqs.extend(d_req_id for d_req_id, _ in waiters.values())
+                    if err_msg is None:
+                        err_msg = "Timeout waiting for P side ready."
+                    for task in waiters:
+                        task.cancel()
+                    waiters.clear()
+                    continue
+
+                for task in done:
+                    d_req_id, send_meta = waiters.pop(task)
+                    if send_meta.aborted.is_set():
+                        err_reqs.append(d_req_id)
+                        if err_msg is None:
+                            err_msg = (
+                                "The prefiller released this request before "
+                                "handing out its blocks."
+                            )
+                        continue
+                    resolved[d_req_id] = (
+                        send_meta.transfer_id,
+                        send_meta.local_block_ids,
+                    )
+                    self._handed_out_readers.setdefault(
+                        send_meta.transfer_id, set()
+                    ).add(readers_key)
+                    self._handed_out_at[send_meta.transfer_id] = time.perf_counter()
+        finally:
+            for task in waiters:
+                task.cancel()
+
+    async def _handle_read_done(
+        self, identity: bytes, sock: zmq.asyncio.Socket, message: MooncakePullDone
+    ) -> None:
+        readers_key: ReaderKey = (message.engine_id, message.tp_rank, message.pp_rank)
+        for transfer_id in message.transfer_ids:
+            send_meta = self.reqs_need_send.get(transfer_id)
+            if send_meta is None:
+                # Already released: every reader of this transfer reported in.
+                continue
+            if message.failed_transfers and transfer_id in message.failed_transfers:
+                logger.warning(
+                    "Reader %s failed to read transfer %s; releasing its blocks.",
+                    readers_key,
+                    transfer_id,
+                )
+            self._mark_reader_done(send_meta, readers_key)
+
+        ack = MooncakePullAck()
+        await sock.send_multipart((identity, self._encoder.encode(ack)))
+
+    ############################################################
+    # Decoder side: read the peer's blocks
+    ############################################################
+
+    async def receive_kv_from_single_worker(
+        self,
+        worker_addr: str,
+        pull_metas: dict[ReqId, PullReqMeta],
+    ):
+        req_ids = set(pull_metas)
+        request = MooncakePullRequest(
+            protocol=PULL_PROTOCOL,
+            compat_hash=self._compat_hash,
+            engine_id=self.engine_id,
+            tp_rank=self.tp_rank,
+            tp_size=self.tp_size,
+            pp_rank=self.pp_rank,
+            pp_size=self.pp_size,
+            reqs={
+                req_id: (
+                    pull_meta.transfer_id,
+                    any(len(group) > 0 for group in pull_meta.local_block_ids),
+                )
+                for req_id, pull_meta in pull_metas.items()
+            },
+            want_layout=worker_addr not in self._peer_layouts,
+        )
+        encoded_data = self._encoder.encode(request)
+        logger.debug(
+            "Reading kv_caches for %s from producer worker %s", req_ids, worker_addr
+        )
+
+        try:
+            with make_zmq_socket(
+                self.async_zmq_ctx, worker_addr, zmq.DEALER, bind=False, linger=0
+            ) as sock:
+                # If something goes wrong, let the prefiller wait for its own
+                # timeout before we give up on the request.
+                sock.setsockopt(
+                    zmq.RCVTIMEO, (envs.VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT + 60) * 1000
+                )
+                await sock.send(encoded_data)
+                while True:
+                    response = self._pull_response_decoder.decode(await sock.recv())
+                    if not await self._handle_pull_response(
+                        sock, worker_addr, pull_metas, response
+                    ):
+                        return
+                    if response.status == MooncakeXferResponseStatus.FINISH:
+                        break
+        except msgspec.DecodeError as e:
+            self._handle_failed_recv(
+                pull_metas,
+                req_ids,
+                f"undecodable response from {worker_addr}: {e}. The peer may run "
+                "another Mooncake connector mode than this decoder.",
+            )
+        except zmq.ContextTerminated:
+            logger.debug("ZMQ context terminated, exiting Mooncake receiver thread.")
+        except Exception as e:
+            self._handle_failed_recv(pull_metas, req_ids, f"pull failed: {e}")
+
+    async def _abandon_batch(
+        self,
+        sock: zmq.asyncio.Socket,
+        pull_metas: dict[ReqId, PullReqMeta],
+        reason: str,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Fail this batch locally, then release the blocks the peer holds.
+
+        The prefiller hands out block ids before the decoder can validate the
+        response, so it holds those blocks until this reader reports in. An
+        abandoned batch has to report as well, or the blocks would wait for the
+        prefiller's own timeout.
+        """
+        self._handle_failed_recv(pull_metas, set(pull_metas), reason)
+        transfer_ids = [meta.transfer_id for meta in pull_metas.values()]
+        done = MooncakePullDone(
+            protocol=PULL_PROTOCOL,
+            engine_id=self.engine_id,
+            tp_rank=self.tp_rank,
+            pp_rank=self.pp_rank,
+            transfer_ids=transfer_ids,
+            failed_transfers=transfer_ids,
+        )
+        await sock.send(self._encoder.encode(done))
+
+    async def _handle_pull_response(
+        self,
+        sock: zmq.asyncio.Socket,
+        worker_addr: str,
+        pull_metas: dict[ReqId, PullReqMeta],
+        response: MooncakePullResponse,
+    ) -> bool:
+        """Act on one prefiller response; False ends this peer's read."""
+        if response.status == MooncakeXferResponseStatus.ERROR:
+            await self._abandon_batch(
+                sock, pull_metas, response.err_msg or "transfer error"
+            )
+            return False
+
+        if response.compat_hash != self._compat_hash:
+            await self._abandon_batch(
+                sock,
+                pull_metas,
+                self._compat_mismatch_reason(response.compat_hash),
+            )
+            return False
+
+        if response.layout is not None:
+            layout_err = self._accept_layout(worker_addr, response.layout)
+            if layout_err is not None:
+                await self._abandon_batch(sock, pull_metas, layout_err)
+                return False
+
+        layout = self._peer_layouts[worker_addr]
+        if response.layout_id and response.layout_id != layout.layout_id:
+            self._peer_layouts.pop(worker_addr)
+            await self._abandon_batch(
+                sock,
+                pull_metas,
+                f"producer worker {worker_addr} changed its KV layout "
+                f"({layout.layout_id} -> {response.layout_id}); it restarted and "
+                "the KV of this request must be recomputed",
+            )
+            return False
+
+        if response.resolved:
+            await self._read_batch(sock, worker_addr, pull_metas, response.resolved)
+
+        if response.err_reqs:
+            self._handle_failed_recv(
+                pull_metas, response.err_reqs, response.err_msg or "unknown error"
+            )
+        return True
+
+    def _accept_layout(
+        self, worker_addr: str, layout: MooncakePullLayout
+    ) -> str | None:
+        """Cache a peer address book, or explain why it cannot be used."""
+        cached = self._peer_layouts.get(worker_addr)
+        if cached is not None:
+            if cached.layout_id != layout.layout_id:
+                # Drop the stale address book so the next request for this peer
+                # asks for the new one instead of failing the same way again.
+                self._peer_layouts.pop(worker_addr)
+                return (
+                    f"producer worker {worker_addr} reports a new KV layout "
+                    f"({cached.layout_id} -> {layout.layout_id}); it restarted, "
+                    "so this request must be recomputed"
+                )
+            return None
+
+        mismatch = self._layout_mismatch_reason(layout)
+        if mismatch is not None:
+            return mismatch
+        self._peer_layouts[worker_addr] = layout
+        return None
+
+    def _layout_mismatch_reason(self, layout: MooncakePullLayout) -> str | None:
+        """Reject address books that cannot describe this worker's own cache."""
+        if layout.block_size != self.block_size:
+            return (
+                f"producer block size {layout.block_size} differs from the local "
+                f"{self.block_size}; a pull needs the same physical block size on "
+                "both sides"
+            )
+        if (
+            layout.physical_blocks_per_logical
+            != self._physical_blocks_per_logical_kv_block
+        ):
+            return (
+                "producer uses "
+                f"{layout.physical_blocks_per_logical} physical blocks per logical "
+                "block while this decoder uses "
+                f"{self._physical_blocks_per_logical_kv_block}"
+            )
+        if layout.use_mla != self.use_mla:
+            return (
+                f"producer use_mla={layout.use_mla} differs from the local "
+                f"{self.use_mla}"
+            )
+        if layout.has_mamba != self.kv_cache_config.has_mamba_layers:
+            return (
+                f"producer has_mamba={layout.has_mamba} differs from the local "
+                f"{self.kv_cache_config.has_mamba_layers}"
+            )
+        return None
+
+    def _peer_transfer_regions(
+        self, layout: MooncakePullLayout
+    ) -> list[TransferRegion]:
+        shared = [tuple(groups) for groups in layout.shared_group_ids]
+        shared_groups = None if len(shared) != len(layout.layer_names) else shared
+        row_offsets = (
+            None
+            if len(layout.row_offsets) != len(layout.layer_names)
+            else layout.row_offsets
+        )
+        return self._get_transfer_regions(
+            base_addrs=layout.kv_caches_base_addr,
+            block_lens=layout.block_lens,
+            kv_block_lens=layout.kv_block_lens,
+            layer_names=layout.layer_names,
+            layer_indices=layout.layer_indices,
+            group_indices=layout.group_indices,
+            shared_group_ids=shared_groups,
+            row_offsets=row_offsets,
+        )
+
+    def _local_transfer_regions(self) -> list[TransferRegion]:
+        registered_layers = len(self.registered_layer_names)
+        shared_groups = (
+            None
+            if len(self.region_shared_groups) != registered_layers
+            else self.region_shared_groups
+        )
+        row_offsets = (
+            None
+            if len(self.region_row_offsets) != registered_layers
+            else self.region_row_offsets
+        )
+        return self._get_transfer_regions(
+            base_addrs=self.kv_caches_base_addr,
+            block_lens=self.block_len_per_layer,
+            kv_block_lens=self.kv_block_len_per_layer,
+            layer_names=self.registered_layer_names,
+            layer_indices=self.registered_layer_indices,
+            group_indices=self.registered_group_indices,
+            shared_group_ids=shared_groups,
+            row_offsets=row_offsets,
+        )
+
+    def _plan_reads(
+        self,
+        layout: MooncakePullLayout,
+        pull_metas: dict[ReqId, PullReqMeta],
+        resolved: dict[ReqId, tuple[TransferId, list[list[int]]]],
+    ) -> tuple[list[int], list[int], list[int], list[ReqId], str | None]:
+        """Plan the reads of one response batch.
+
+        Returns:
+            Local pointers to read into, remote pointers to read from, lengths,
+            requests that failed planning, and the failure reason.
+
+        """
+        producer_regions = self._peer_transfer_regions(layout)
+        consumer_regions = self._local_transfer_regions()
+        producer_regions, consumer_regions, align_err = _align_transfer_regions(
+            producer_regions,
+            consumer_regions,
+            allow_partial_layers=(
+                layout.pp_size > 1 and layout.pp_size != self.pp_size
+            ),
+        )
+        if align_err is not None:
+            return [], [], [], list(resolved), align_err
+
+        total_num_kv_heads = (
+            None
+            if self.use_mla or self.kv_cache_config.has_mamba_layers
+            else self.transfer_topo.total_num_kv_heads
+        )
+        validation_err = _validate_asymmetric_region_lengths(
+            local_regions=producer_regions,
+            remote_regions=consumer_regions,
+            local_tp_size=layout.tp_size,
+            remote_tp_size=self.tp_size,
+            producer_cache_replicated=layout.producer_cache_replicated,
+            total_num_kv_heads=total_num_kv_heads,
+        )
+        if validation_err is not None:
+            return [], [], [], list(resolved), validation_err
+
+        requests = [
+            ReadRequest(
+                key=d_req_id,
+                producer_block_ids=producer_block_ids,
+                consumer_block_ids=pull_metas[d_req_id].local_block_ids,
+            )
+            for d_req_id, (_, producer_block_ids) in resolved.items()
+            if d_req_id in pull_metas
+        ]
+
+        def plan(
+            producer_region: TransferRegion, consumer_region: TransferRegion
+        ) -> tuple[bool, int, int, int]:
+            # Plan the copy from the prefiller's side: it owns the bytes.
+            return _compute_sender_transfer_plan(
+                local_tp_rank=layout.tp_rank,
+                local_tp_size=layout.tp_size,
+                remote_tp_rank=self.tp_rank,
+                remote_tp_size=self.tp_size,
+                local_kv_block_len=producer_region.kv_block_len,
+                remote_kv_block_len=consumer_region.kv_block_len,
+                producer_cache_replicated=layout.producer_cache_replicated,
+                total_num_kv_heads=total_num_kv_heads,
+            )
+
+        # The prefiller holds the bytes, so its blocks are the remote side.
+        local_ptrs, remote_ptrs, lengths, err_reqs, err_msg = (
+            plan_read_block_descriptors(
+                requests,
+                producer_regions=producer_regions,
+                consumer_regions=consumer_regions,
+                group_specs=self.kv_cache_config.transfer_groups,
+                producer_blocks_per_logical=layout.physical_blocks_per_logical,
+                consumer_blocks_per_logical=self._physical_blocks_per_logical_kv_block,
+                plan=plan,
+            )
+        )
+        return local_ptrs, remote_ptrs, lengths, err_reqs, err_msg
+
+    async def _read_batch(
+        self,
+        sock: zmq.asyncio.Socket,
+        worker_addr: str,
+        pull_metas: dict[ReqId, PullReqMeta],
+        resolved: dict[ReqId, tuple[TransferId, list[list[int]]]],
+    ) -> None:
+        """Read one response batch and report it back to the prefiller."""
+        layout = self._peer_layouts[worker_addr]
+        (
+            local_ptrs,
+            remote_ptrs,
+            lengths,
+            err_reqs,
+            err_msg,
+        ) = self._plan_reads(layout, pull_metas, resolved)
+
+        failed_transfers: list[TransferId] = []
+        if err_reqs:
+            failed_set = set(err_reqs)
+            self._handle_failed_recv(
+                pull_metas, err_reqs, err_msg or "read planning failed"
+            )
+            failed_transfers.extend(
+                transfer_id
+                for d_req_id, (transfer_id, _) in resolved.items()
+                if d_req_id in failed_set
+            )
+
+        if local_ptrs:
+            remote_session = f"{layout.hostname}:{layout.rpc_port}"
+            ret_value = await asyncio.get_running_loop().run_in_executor(
+                self._reader_executor,
+                self._read_blocks,
+                remote_session,
+                local_ptrs,
+                remote_ptrs,
+                lengths,
+            )
+            if ret_value != 0:
+                # Every request in this batch shares the failed engine call.
+                read_reqs = [
+                    d_req_id
+                    for d_req_id, (_, producer_blocks) in resolved.items()
+                    if any(len(group) > 0 for group in producer_blocks)
+                    and d_req_id in pull_metas
+                ]
+                read_req_set = set(read_reqs)
+                self._handle_failed_recv(
+                    pull_metas,
+                    read_reqs,
+                    f"Mooncake transfer engine returned {ret_value}",
+                )
+                failed_transfers.extend(
+                    transfer_id
+                    for d_req_id, (transfer_id, _) in resolved.items()
+                    if d_req_id in read_req_set
+                )
+
+        # Report the batch so the prefiller can release these blocks.
+        done = MooncakePullDone(
+            protocol=PULL_PROTOCOL,
+            engine_id=self.engine_id,
+            tp_rank=self.tp_rank,
+            pp_rank=self.pp_rank,
+            transfer_ids=[transfer_id for transfer_id, _ in resolved.values()],
+            failed_transfers=failed_transfers or None,
+        )
+        await sock.send(self._encoder.encode(done))
+        ack = self._pull_ack_decoder.decode(await sock.recv())
+        if not ack.ok:
+            logger.warning(
+                "Producer worker %s did not acknowledge the read of %s",
+                worker_addr,
+                list(resolved),
+            )
+
+        for d_req_id in resolved:
+            pull_meta = pull_metas.get(d_req_id)
+            if pull_meta is None or pull_meta.failed:
+                continue
+            # No race because we are in the async loop.
+            pull_meta.pull_tasks_count -= 1
+            # Empty pulls only release the producer's blocks; the consumer did
+            # not enter WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS.
+            if pull_meta.pull_tasks_count == 0 and any(pull_meta.local_block_ids):
+                self.finished_recving_reqs.add(pull_meta.d_req_id)
+
+    def _read_blocks(
+        self,
+        remote_session: str,
+        local_ptrs: list[int],
+        remote_ptrs: list[int],
+        lengths: list[int],
+    ) -> int:
+        start_time = time.perf_counter()
+        ret_value = self.engine.batch_transfer_sync_read(
+            remote_session, local_ptrs, remote_ptrs, lengths
+        )
+        duration = time.perf_counter() - start_time
+        if ret_value == 0:
+            self.xfer_stats.record_transfer(
+                duration_s=duration,
+                total_bytes=sum(lengths),
+                num_descs=len(local_ptrs),
+            )
+            logger.debug(
+                "Reading from %s done, took %s (%d descriptors, %d bytes)",
+                remote_session,
+                duration,
+                len(local_ptrs),
+                sum(lengths),
+            )
+        else:
+            self.xfer_stats.record_failed_transfer()
+            logger.warning(
+                "Reading from %s failed (ret=%s) after %s (%d descriptors, %d bytes)",
+                remote_session,
+                ret_value,
+                duration,
+                len(local_ptrs),
+                sum(lengths),
+            )
+        return ret_value

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Read-side descriptor planning for the Mooncake pull connector.
+
+`MooncakeConnectorWorker` turns a decoder's block table into source and
+destination descriptors and writes them. A pull connector needs the same plan
+with the two sides swapped, because the decoder reads the prefiller's bytes into
+its own cache: the prefiller's blocks are the remote descriptors and the
+decoder's blocks are the local ones. This module builds that plan from the same
+registered regions.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake.mooncake_connector import (
+    ReqId,
+    TransferRegion,
+    _block_ids_for_region,
+    _can_coalesce_block_transfers,
+    group_concurrent_contiguous,
+)
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import NULL_BLOCK_ID
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import KVCacheGroupSpec, MambaSpec
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+TransferPlan = Callable[[TransferRegion, TransferRegion], tuple[bool, int, int, int]]
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ReadRequest:
+    """One request's blocks on both sides of a read.
+
+    Attributes:
+        key: Request id the caller uses to report failures.
+        producer_block_ids: Per KV group, the blocks holding the KV to read.
+        consumer_block_ids: Per KV group, the local blocks to read it into.
+
+    """
+
+    key: ReqId
+    producer_block_ids: list[list[int]]
+    consumer_block_ids: list[list[int]]
+
+
+def _kernel_block_ids(
+    block_ids: list[list[int]],
+    group_specs: Sequence[KVCacheGroupSpec],
+    blocks_per_logical: int,
+) -> list[list[int]]:
+    """Expand logical block ids to the kernel blocks serving them.
+
+    A logical block served by several attention kernel blocks expands to all of
+    them, while a Mamba/GDN state block keeps its logical id.
+    """
+    if blocks_per_logical == 1:
+        return block_ids
+
+    block_arange = np.arange(blocks_per_logical).reshape(1, -1)
+    return [
+        (
+            (np.array(group)[:, None] * blocks_per_logical + block_arange)
+            .reshape(-1)
+            .tolist()
+            if not isinstance(group_specs[index].kv_cache_spec, MambaSpec)
+            else group
+        )
+        for index, group in enumerate(block_ids)
+    ]
+
+
+def _drop_mamba_placeholders(
+    block_ids: list[list[int]], group_specs: Sequence[KVCacheGroupSpec]
+) -> list[list[int]]:
+    """Drop null blocks, which are prefix-cache placeholders without state."""
+    return [
+        (
+            [block_id for block_id in group if block_id != NULL_BLOCK_ID]
+            if isinstance(group_specs[index].kv_cache_spec, MambaSpec)
+            else group
+        )
+        for index, group in enumerate(block_ids)
+    ]
+
+
+def plan_read_block_descriptors(
+    requests: Sequence[ReadRequest],
+    *,
+    producer_regions: Sequence[TransferRegion],
+    consumer_regions: Sequence[TransferRegion],
+    group_specs: Sequence[KVCacheGroupSpec],
+    producer_blocks_per_logical: int,
+    consumer_blocks_per_logical: int,
+    plan: TransferPlan,
+) -> tuple[list[int], list[int], list[int], list[ReqId], str | None]:
+    """Plan one read per request into local and remote descriptor lists.
+
+    Args:
+        requests: Requests to read, each carrying both sides' block ids.
+        producer_regions: Aligned regions of the prefiller's KV cache.
+        consumer_regions: Aligned regions of this decoder's KV cache.
+        group_specs: KV cache groups of this instance.
+        producer_blocks_per_logical: Kernel blocks per logical block on the peer.
+        consumer_blocks_per_logical: Kernel blocks per logical block locally.
+        plan: Callback returning the transfer flag, the producer byte offset,
+            the consumer byte offset and the copy length for one region pair.
+
+    Returns:
+        Local (decoder) descriptors, remote (prefiller) descriptors, lengths,
+        the request ids that cannot be read, and the reason for those failures.
+
+    """
+    local_ptrs: list[int] = []
+    remote_ptrs: list[int] = []
+    lengths: list[int] = []
+    err_reqs: list[ReqId] = []
+    err_msg: str | None = None
+
+    for request in requests:
+        if not any(request.producer_block_ids) or not any(request.consumer_block_ids):
+            # An empty read only releases the prefiller's blocks.
+            continue
+
+        if len(request.producer_block_ids) != len(request.consumer_block_ids):
+            logger.error(
+                "req %s: KV group count mismatch: producer=%d, consumer=%d",
+                request.key,
+                len(request.producer_block_ids),
+                len(request.consumer_block_ids),
+            )
+            err_reqs.append(request.key)
+            if err_msg is None:
+                err_msg = "KV group count mismatch"
+            continue
+
+        assert len(request.consumer_block_ids) == len(group_specs), (
+            "A read must carry one block list per local KV cache group."
+        )
+
+        producer_groups = _drop_mamba_placeholders(
+            request.producer_block_ids, group_specs
+        )
+        consumer_groups = _drop_mamba_placeholders(
+            request.consumer_block_ids, group_specs
+        )
+
+        trimmed_producer: list[list[int]] = []
+        trimmed_consumer: list[list[int]] = []
+        for producer_group, consumer_group in zip(producer_groups, consumer_groups):
+            if len(producer_group) < len(consumer_group):
+                logger.error(
+                    "req %s: producer blocks(%d) < consumer blocks(%d) in a KV "
+                    "cache group",
+                    request.key,
+                    len(producer_group),
+                    len(consumer_group),
+                )
+                err_reqs.append(request.key)
+                if err_msg is None:
+                    err_msg = "producer num blocks less than consumer"
+                break
+            if len(producer_group) > len(consumer_group):
+                # The decoder already holds a prefix, so its read covers the
+                # last blocks of the prefiller's request.
+                producer_group = (
+                    producer_group[-len(consumer_group) :] if consumer_group else []
+                )
+            trimmed_producer.append(producer_group)
+            trimmed_consumer.append(consumer_group)
+        else:
+            producer_groups, consumer_groups = trimmed_producer, trimmed_consumer
+
+        if err_reqs and err_reqs[-1] == request.key:
+            continue
+
+        producer_groups = _kernel_block_ids(
+            producer_groups, group_specs, producer_blocks_per_logical
+        )
+        consumer_groups = _kernel_block_ids(
+            consumer_groups, group_specs, consumer_blocks_per_logical
+        )
+
+        for producer_region, consumer_region in zip(producer_regions, consumer_regions):
+            assert producer_region.group_index == consumer_region.group_index, (
+                "Aligned Mooncake transfer regions must belong to the same KV group."
+            )
+            producer_block_ids = _block_ids_for_region(
+                producer_groups,
+                producer_region.group_index,
+                producer_region.shared_group_ids,
+            )
+            consumer_block_ids = _block_ids_for_region(
+                consumer_groups,
+                consumer_region.group_index,
+                consumer_region.shared_group_ids,
+            )
+            if not consumer_block_ids:
+                continue
+
+            grouped_producer_blocks, grouped_consumer_blocks = (
+                group_concurrent_contiguous(producer_block_ids, consumer_block_ids)
+            )
+            (
+                should_transfer,
+                producer_offset,
+                consumer_offset,
+                transfer_len,
+            ) = plan(producer_region, consumer_region)
+            if not should_transfer:
+                # A replicated prefiller cache: another rank holds these bytes.
+                continue
+
+            assert producer_offset + transfer_len <= producer_region.kv_block_len, (
+                "Computed read offset exceeds the producer KV block size."
+            )
+            assert consumer_offset + transfer_len <= consumer_region.kv_block_len, (
+                "Computed read offset exceeds the consumer KV block size."
+            )
+            # Collapse one contiguous block group into a single larger
+            # descriptor when the per-block copy is identical.
+            can_coalesce = _can_coalesce_block_transfers(
+                local_region_block_len=producer_region.block_len,
+                remote_region_block_len=consumer_region.block_len,
+                src_region_offset=producer_offset,
+                dst_region_offset=consumer_offset,
+                transfer_len=transfer_len,
+            )
+
+            for producer_blocks, consumer_blocks in zip(
+                grouped_producer_blocks, grouped_consumer_blocks
+            ):
+                if can_coalesce:
+                    remote_ptrs.append(
+                        producer_region.base_addr
+                        + producer_blocks[0] * producer_region.block_len
+                        + producer_offset
+                    )
+                    local_ptrs.append(
+                        consumer_region.base_addr
+                        + consumer_blocks[0] * consumer_region.block_len
+                        + consumer_offset
+                    )
+                    lengths.append(transfer_len * len(consumer_blocks))
+                else:
+                    for producer_block, consumer_block in zip(
+                        producer_blocks, consumer_blocks
+                    ):
+                        remote_ptrs.append(
+                            producer_region.base_addr
+                            + producer_block * producer_region.block_len
+                            + producer_offset
+                        )
+                        local_ptrs.append(
+                            consumer_region.base_addr
+                            + consumer_block * consumer_region.block_len
+                            + consumer_offset
+                        )
+                        lengths.append(transfer_len)
+
+    return local_ptrs, remote_ptrs, lengths, err_reqs, err_msg
